design.text: Randomized (1:1), international, open-label, multicenter trial of tislelizumab 200 mg IV Q3W versus investigator's choice of chemotherapy (paclitaxel, docetaxel, or irinotecan).

citations.quote: RATIONALE-302 (NCT03430843) is a randomized, international, open-label trial in patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) with disease progression on/after previous therapy.

- Tislelizumab 200 mg intravenously (IV) every 3 weeks (Q3W)
- Investigator's choice of chemotherapy: paclitaxel (135 mg/m2 IV Q3W), docetaxel (75 mg/m2 IV Q3W), or irinotecan (125 mg/m2 IV on Days 1 and 8 of every 3-week cycle). Regional variations on dosing regimen for taxanes were allowed.

population.text: Adults with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic ESCC with disease progression on/after prior therapy, irrespective of PD-L1 status, ECOG PS 0 or 1; prior PD-1/PD-L1 antibody therapy excluded.

citations.quote: Patients were eligible if they had histologically confirmed predominant squamous cell histology, irrespective of PD-L1 status, and ECOG PS of 0 or 1.
Patients with prior therapy with PD-1 or PD-L1 monoclonal antibodies were not eligible for the trial.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint was overall survival (OS) in all patients; key secondary endpoint was OS in patients with PD-L1 ≥ 10%.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint of the trial was overall survival (OS) in all patients; the key secondary endpoint was OS in patients with PD-L1 \ge 10\%.

As of the data cutoff date of 01 December 2020, a total of 512 patients were randomized to the Tislelizumab Arm (256 patients) and the ICC Arm (256 patients), with the last patient randomized on 04 March 2020.

result.text: OS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.57, 0.85; one-sided p = 0.0001); median OS 8.6 months (tislelizumab) vs 6.3 months (ICC). ORR 20.3% vs 9.8%; PFS HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.67, 1.01).

citations.quote: The OS HR in the ITT was 0.70 (95% CI 0.57, 0.85; one-sided p-value = 0.0001) with a median OS of 8.6 months (95% CI 7.5, 10.4) in the tislelizumab arm
and 6.3 months (95% CI 5.3, 7) in the ICC arm.
The ORR was 20.3% (95% CI 15.6, 25.8) in the tislelizumab arm and 9.8% (95% CI 6.4, 14.1) in the ICC arm.
The HR for PFS in the ITT was 0.83 (95% CI 0.67, 1.01).

target_moa.text: Monoclonal antibody that binds PD-1 and blocks its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing PD-1/PD-L1-mediated inhibition of the immune response and activating anti-tumor immunity.

citations.quote: Tislelizumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds to programmed-death receptor 1 (PD-1) and blocks its interactions with both its ligands. This releases the PD-1/PD-L1-mediated inhibition of the immune response, including activation of the anti-tumor immune response.

Tislelizumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds to programmed-death receptor 1 (PD-1) and blocks its interactions with both its ligands. This releases the PD-1/PD-L1-mediated inhibition of the immune response, including activation of the anti-tumor immune response.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%, including lab abnormalities): increased glucose, decreased hemoglobin, decreased lymphocytes, decreased sodium, decreased albumin, increased alkaline phosphatase, anemia, fatigue, increased AST, musculoskeletal pain, decreased weight, increased ALT, and cough. Immune-mediated adverse events occurred in 21% of tislelizumab patients (Grade ≥3 in 4%); most frequent were hypothyroidism (9%) and pneumonitis (7%). Permanent discontinuation due to an adverse reaction occurred in 19%.

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (\ge 20%), including laboratory abnormalities with TEVIMBRA were: increased glucose, decreased hemoglobin, decreased lymphocytes, decreased sodium, decreased albumin, increased alkaline phosphatase, anemia, fatigue, increased AST, musculoskeletal pain, decreased weight, increased ALT, and cough. (6,1)

The primary risks of tislelizumab are immune-mediated adverse events (imAEs), which were reported in 21% patients receiving tislelizumab. Most of the imAEs were Grade 1-2, and the incidence of Grade \ge 3 imAEs was 4%.
The most frequently reported imAEs were hypothyroidism (9%) and pneumonitis (7%).
Permanent discontinuation of tislelizumab due to an adverse reaction occurred in 19% of patients.

detail.text: No REMS required; no safety issues identified requiring a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy.

citations.quote: There are no safety issues identified at this time requiring Risk Evaluation and Mitigations Strategies. Tislelizumab is the 8th approved PD-1/PD-L1 targeting monoclonal antibody and the second in class for the treatment of patients with ESCC with relapsed/refractory disease.
